task: COSO Citation Mapping — 38 Domain E Seeds
methodology: For each seed, analyzed stem, topic, LOS, blueprint-assigned COSO_Principle, and current EC text. Mapped primary principle to the single most relevant COSO Internal Control (2013) Principle or COSO ERM component. Supporting principles are those also relevant but not the primary focus. Checked each EC for explicit COSO/ERM citation text.

internal_control_2013.P1: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values
internal_control_2013.P11: Selects and develops general controls over technology

coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 10, control activities including segregation of duties help ensure that management's directives to mitigate risks are carried out. Principle 12 further requires that these controls be deployed through policies and procedures.

coso_citation_map.primary_name: COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework (all 17 principles across 5 components)
coso_citation_map.citation_text: The COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework (2013) is built on five integrated components — control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, and monitoring — supported by 17 principles that together provide a comprehensive structure for evaluating internal control effectiveness.
coso_citation_map.note: EC already names COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework and lists all five components. Citation is adequate for certification.

coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 8, organizations must assess the potential for fraud in achieving objectives by considering the fraud triangle elements: pressure, opportunity, and rationalization.

Under COSO Principle 10, physical safeguarding controls over assets are a category of control activities designed to limit access to authorized personnel and protect organizational resources from unauthorized use, damage, or loss.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.021 segregation of duties vendor setup and payment
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 10, segregation of duties is a fundamental control activity that separates incompatible functions — such as vendor creation and payment approval — to reduce the risk of fraud or error going undetected.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.022 preventive vs detective duplicate payment control
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, general controls over technology include automated application controls such as duplicate-check validation, which is a preventive control that blocks erroneous or fraudulent transactions before they are processed.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.023 IT access control terminated employee deprovisioning
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, general controls over technology include access management processes such as automated deprovisioning, which ensures that system access is promptly revoked upon employee termination to prevent unauthorized data exposure or processing.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.024 application input control sales order validation
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, application controls such as real-time field validation are technology-based control activities that check data for completeness, validity, and reasonableness at the point of entry to prevent processing errors.

Under COSO Principle 10, preventive control activities such as dual-signature authorization are designed to stop errors or irregularities before they occur, in contrast with detective controls that identify issues after the fact.

Under COSO Principle 16, ongoing monitoring activities such as independent bank reconciliations evaluate whether controls are functioning as intended by comparing recorded amounts to external, independent sources of information.

Under the COSO Enterprise Risk Management — Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017) framework, risk appetite is the amount and type of risk an organization is willing to accept in pursuit of its strategic objectives, defined by the board through the Strategy & Objective-Setting component.

coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, general controls over technology include periodic review of user access rights, which supports the principle of least privilege by ensuring access remains appropriate for current job responsibilities.

coso_citation_map.primary_name: COSO Internal Control — Inherent Limitation (applies to all 17 principles)
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under the COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework, management override of established controls is an inherent limitation of any internal control system. Even well-designed controls (Principles 10–12) can be bypassed when senior management exerts pressure, underscoring the importance of a strong control environment (Principle 1).

Under COSO Principle 14, internal communication channels such as anonymous whistleblower hotlines provide mechanisms for employees to report suspected misconduct, supporting the information and communication component of internal control and reinforcing fraud-risk monitoring under Principle 8.

Under COSO Principle 10, when full segregation of duties is not feasible — as in small organizations — compensating control activities such as active management review of transactions can mitigate the resulting risk. The COSO framework recognizes that control activities should be scaled to the organization's size and complexity.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.060 control environment tone at top
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 1, the control environment — including tone at the top — is the foundation of internal control. When the board and senior management demonstrate a commitment to integrity and ethical values, it sets expectations that influence employee attitudes and behavior throughout the organization.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.061 inherent risk vs control risk
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 7, organizations must identify and analyze risks to the achievement of objectives. Inherent risk represents the susceptibility of an assertion to material misstatement before considering related controls, distinguishing it from control risk which reflects the risk that controls fail to prevent or detect the misstatement.

Under COSO Principle 10, segregation of incompatible duties — such as separating cash custody (asset handling) from cash receipt recording (recordkeeping) — is a foundational control activity that reduces the risk of misappropriation and concealment.

Under COSO Principle 17, organizations must evaluate internal control deficiencies and communicate corrective actions to parties responsible for remediation. Assigning an owner, action plan, and target completion date operationalizes this principle by creating accountability for timely correction.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.001 three lines of defense model
coso_citation_map.primary_name: COSO Internal Control — Governance Structure (P1-P5 broadly)
coso_citation_map.citation_text: The Three Lines Model assigns control responsibilities across operational management (first line — owns controls), risk and compliance oversight (second line — provides guidance), and internal audit (third line — delivers independent assurance). Under the COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework, this governance structure supports oversight responsibility (Principle 2) and the establishment of authority and responsibility (Principle 3).

coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, general controls over technology include the principle of least privilege — limiting each user's system access to only what is necessary for their current job duties — which reduces the risk of unauthorized processing, data exposure, or misuse.

Under COSO Principle 10, independent verification is a control activity in which a second person reviews work performed by another to check for accuracy and completeness. This detective control provides an objective check before results are finalized.

Under the COSO Enterprise Risk Management — Integrating with Strategy and Performance (2017) framework, risk response strategies fall within the Performance component. Purchasing insurance is a form of risk transfer, shifting the financial consequences of a risk to a third party rather than accepting, avoiding, or reducing the risk.

Under COSO Principle 10, authorization controls — such as requiring manager approval before high-dollar purchase orders are placed — are preventive control activities that ensure transactions are properly sanctioned before the organization becomes obligated.

Under COSO Principle 16, ongoing monitoring evaluations involve the periodic review of exception reports and reconciliations as part of regular operations to assess whether controls continue to function as intended over time. This differs from transaction-level controls in that it evaluates, rather than executes, the control.

coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, general controls over technology include business continuity and disaster recovery planning, which addresses the availability objective of information systems by ensuring that critical financial data and processing capabilities can be restored after a disruption.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.036 change management control it systems
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, change management controls are a category of IT general controls that govern how modifications to information systems are approved, tested, documented, and migrated to production. These controls protect the integrity, availability, and reliability of financial data.

Under COSO Principle 7, risk identification and analysis involves assessing the likelihood and potential impact of risks to the achievement of objectives. Scoring risks by likelihood and impact enables management to prioritize which exposures warrant the most immediate attention.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.046 code of conduct ethics program
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Demonstrates commitment to integrity and ethical values
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 1, the organization demonstrates a commitment to integrity and ethical values through actions such as establishing a code of conduct, requiring annual ethics training, and holding employees accountable for adherence. This reinforces the control environment as the foundation of internal control.

coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, general controls over technology include authentication controls such as multi-factor authentication, which strengthens access security by requiring multiple forms of verification before granting system access to financial data.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.058 internal control cost benefit limitation
coso_citation_map.primary_name: COSO Internal Control — Inherent Limitation (cost-benefit applies to all 17 principles)
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under the COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework, internal control has inherent limitations including the cost-benefit constraint: controls should provide reasonable, not absolute, assurance. Declining an extremely costly control for a low-frequency risk reflects management's judgment that the cost of the control exceeds its expected risk-reduction benefit.

Under COSO Principle 10, segregation of duties between vendor-master-file maintenance and invoice-payment approval is a control activity that reduces the risk of fictitious-vendor schemes and payment diversion. This control also supports Principle 8's requirement to assess and address fraud risk.

Under COSO Principle 2, the board of directors exercises oversight responsibility for the system of internal control, including through its audit committee, which provides independent oversight of financial reporting integrity, external auditor relationships, and the internal audit function.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.071 change management control direct production change
coso_citation_map.primary_name: Selects and develops general controls over technology
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 11, change management is an IT general control that governs how modifications to information systems are approved, tested, documented, and migrated from development to production. Making an untested, unauthorized change directly to a production system represents a significant internal control deficiency.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.072 fraud risk purchasing conflict of interest
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 8, organizations must assess the potential for fraud, including conflicts of interest in purchasing where a single individual can both create vendors and award contracts. Principle 10 controls — such as independent approval of new vendors and bid awards — address this identified fraud risk.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.073 monitoring exception reports not reviewed
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 16, detective controls such as exception reports are only effective when the exceptions identified are reviewed and acted upon. Generating reports without assigning responsibility for review and follow-up is a monitoring failure that can cause control deficiencies to go unresolved — directly undermining Principle 17.

coso_citation_map.topic: E.074 reconciliation incompatible duties EFT and bank rec
coso_citation_map.citation_text: Under COSO Principle 10, segregation of duties requires that incompatible functions be separated. Combining electronic funds transfer initiation with bank account reconciliation creates a concealment risk — the same employee could initiate unauthorized transfers and hide them by manipulating the reconciliation.

Under COSO Principle 10, separating vendor invoice approval from accounts payable reconciliation is a segregation-of-duties control activity that provides an independent check on the accuracy and authorization of recorded liabilities.

P13 (Relevant Information) — zero seeds as primary
summary.recommendation: 37 of 38 seeds (97%) lack any COSO citation in their ExplanationCorrect fields. During S810.1 remediation, the citation_text provided for each seed should be appended or integrated into the EC as a final sentence or paragraph. The most common principle is P10 (Control Activities), covering 12 SoD/authorization/verification seeds. P11 covers 8 IT control seeds. Only 1 seed (EC-008 — COSO framework overview) already carries an explicit citation. All citations align with the primary COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework (2013) except EC-031 and ED-016 which align with COSO ERM (2017).
